title: Enterprise AI Copilot - product roadmap and Month-1 MVP sprint
refined_problem: The repository is ready (harness operational, README published) but the product itself is undefined as executable work. The owner's original plan defines a 90-day, ~100-hour enterprise AI assistant project (8h/week): a multi-tenant, source-grounded assistant over internal documents with verifiable citations, abstention on insufficient evidence, controlled actions with confirmation, automatic evaluation, and AWS deployment with observability and cost control. We need the roadmap formalized as durable planning artifacts (3 month-level epics, a Month-1 MVP sprint of concrete tasks with acceptance criteria and file surfaces) so future sessions execute rather than re-discuss.

original_request.text: podrias hacer los sprint o spec o lo que quieras que sea necesario para empezar el proyecto y que este todo definido, aunque puedan que arranquen tareas a futuro o ideas, pero para ya tener un roadmap: (plan completo de 90 dias: Mes1 MVP semanas1-4 repositorio/API FastAPI/LLM/carga de documentos/RAG respuestas con sources/frontend basico y demo; Mes2 produccion semanas5-8 auth/separacion de empresas/seguridad pruebas/despliegue AWS Terraform o CDK CI-CD evaluaciones logs metricas; Mes3 portfolio semanas9-13 integracion tickets con confirmacion optimizacion documentacion pruebas seguridad costos demo en ingles) (aprox 8hs semanales, ~100hs totales) (prioridad: producto pequeno y confiable antes que caracteristicas incompletas)

target_users: Internal employees of a tenant company (chat users)
No external multi-tenant *network* exposure beyond one deployed SaaS instance
outcomes: Month 1: working MVP - upload test documents and consult them from a basic chat interface with grounded, cited answers and abstention
Month 2: deployed and evaluated application with verifiable security controls (auth, tenant separation, isolation tests, IaC, CI/CD, logs/metrics)
Month 3: portfolio-grade package - ticket integration with confirmation, optimization, security review, cost report, English demo
Every phase leaves durable evidence: tests, evaluation results, cost data, architecture decisions
success_metrics: MVP demo: question about an uploaded test document answered with correct section citation
Abstention: >=90% of non-evidence questions correctly answered with insufficient-evidence instead of hallucinated content (judged by the evaluation set)
Retrieval quality: >=80% of evaluation questions recover the expected source section in top-5
Month-2 deliverable deployed URL + auth + tenant isolation test suite green
Month-3 deliverable: cost report + latency p50/p95 + 3-5 minute English demo recorded

in: Backend FastAPI (health, documents, chat/answer, actions endpoints)
RAG retrieval with citations and abstention (Bedrock Knowledge Bases candidate vs custom RAG: decided in spike/decisions artifacts)
Document storage abstraction (local for dev, S3 for deployment)
Basic frontend (Next.js) chat + sources display + doc list
Evaluation harness (golden Q&A set, scoring, regression gate)
Auth + multi-tenant separation with automated isolation tests (Month 2)
Mock/demo ticket integration with confirmation flow (Month 3)
English documentation, architecture diagram, portfolio demo
out: Real production enterprise integrations (only a mock/demo ticket system)
Custom vector store infrastructure beyond what the RAG decision requires
Full administration console UI (only minimal upload/list)

mvp.goal: A single-tenant, locally-runnable (but production-shaped) FastAPI+Next.js assistant that ingests test documents and answers with citations or abstains, wired to the evaluation harness. Priority: a small reliable product over incomplete features.
includes: LLM client wrapper (Bedrock) with fake-client tests
Document upload + storage abstraction (local dev, S3-ready)
RAG answer flow with citations and abstention
Evaluation harness skeleton with golden Q&A cases
Minimal Next.js chat UI with sources panel

success_metrics_note: Metric definitions live with the evaluation harness task (MVP-EVAL-001); numbers above are targets, not guarantees.
assumptions: Owner has ~8h/week for 13 weeks (~100h); sprint capacity must stay small
AWS account exists or will be created before Month-2 deployment; costs during MVP are near zero because dev runs locally with fake/mocked clients
SaaS B2B framing is for the portfolio; real customers are not required
Bedrock access: the LLM wrapper must be testable without AWS credentials (fake client by default)
Golden evaluation set will start small (5-10 questions) and grow with each milestone

open_questions.question: Which AWS region/cost ceiling is acceptable for Month-2 (needs operator decision before deployment, not before MVP)?
Which demo ticket system do we integrate in Month 3 (mock-first; real Jira/Linear decision deferred)?
Is the final SaaS-fronted domain name decided (needed only at Month-2 deployment)?

challenges: Abstention threshold tuning: too strict raises unanswered rate, too loose hallucinates; the evaluation harness is the arbiter
Tenant isolation must be enforced in retrieval and backend, with adversarial tests; cannot rely on prompt instructions
AWS costs for Bedrock/KBs during eval; budget guard and cost-per-operation logging early
8h/week limit: every task must be completable in 1-2 evening sessions with clear acceptance
Bedrock KB citations quality vs custom index control; decision is reversible and spike-driven

work_items.title: Month 1 - MVP: functional loop
work_items.description: Weeks 1-2: repo backend, FastAPI API, LLM integration, document loading. Weeks 3-4: RAG with cited answers, evaluation harness, basic frontend, first demo. Deliverable: upload test documents and consult them from an interface. Features: backend bootstrap, LLM client, document ingest, RAG+abstention, eval harness, minimal chat UI.

work_items.title: Month 2 - Production: prototype to enterprise solution
work_items.description: Weeks 5-6: authentication, tenant separation, protection against unauthorized access, security tests. Weeks 7-8: AWS deployment with Terraform/CDK IaC, CI/CD, evaluations gate, logs and metrics. Deliverable: deployed, evaluated application with verifiable security controls. Future sprint planning will materialize its tasks only after this epic's discovery-approved state is used for sprint-planning.

work_items.title: Month 3 - Portfolio: agents, integration and professional demo
work_items.description: Weeks 9-10: demo ticket system integration with confirmation-gated actions. Weeks 11-12: optimization, architecture documentation, security tests, cost analysis. Week 13: English technical demo and business-case presentation. Deliverable: documented repo, demo, metrics, justified architecture decisions.

work_items.title: RAG backend selection spike (Bedrock Knowledge Bases vs custom)
work_items.description: Bounded investigation before MVP-RAG-001: build a minimal retriever interface prototype and compare Bedrock Knowledge Bases (native retrieval+generation+citations) against a custom RAG (embeddings + vector index) on cost per query, index update flow/latency and citation controllability. Output: decision recorded in planning/decisions + program the MVP-RAG-001 task with the chosen contract. Time-boxes: 1 evening session; if defer needed, default to Bedrock KBs for v1 with the local retrieval contract as fallback for testing.

tasks.title: FastAPI backend skeleton with /health and tests
tasks.description: Create the FastAPI application skeleton (backend/app) with: /health endpoint returning service status/version; pydantic settings loaded from environment (APP port/prefix); unittest-discoverCompatible pytest suite (unittest.TestCase style, runnable by both pytest and python -m unittest discover) for /health asserting 200 OK and version field; no external calls; pinned dependencies recorded in backend/pyproject.toml.
acceptance_criteria: GET /health returns 200 with JSON containing status and version fields

Test suite for /health passes locally in unittest-discover form (python -m unittest discover -s tests -v from backend/) and is also runnable via pytest; pure pytest-only styles that unittest discovery would skip silently are not accepted
No AWS/network calls from the health endpoint or its tests
Python package layout with pinned dependencies in backend/pyproject.toml and README development section with run instructions
Tests import the app via explicit sys.path insertion of the backend directory so they pass under the deterministic checker's sanitized environment

tasks.title: Bedrock LLM client wrapper with fake-client tests
tasks.description: Implement backend/app/llm.py: a small client wrapper around AWS Bedrock (converse API) with dependency injection so tests run a fake client by default; model id and region from environment-backed settings; structured answer() returning text plus usage/metadata; this unit performs no identity-material handling: the underlying runtime configuration is an integration-stage concern documented in backend/README; optional integration flag documented and default-off.
acceptance_criteria: wrapper returns a structured LLMResult including text, model_id and usage tokens
unit tests pass with a fake/injectable client, zero network
settings read BEDROCK_MODEL_ID/AWS_REGION via environment with safe defaults and no identity material committed in code or repository
integration flag AWS_INTEGRATION=0/1 documented, integration test skipped unless enabled

tasks.title: Document upload API with storage abstraction
tasks.description: backend/app/documents.py: POST /documents (multipart upload: pdf/md/txt, max size 5 MB by configurable constant), stores content via a StorageBackend abstraction (LocalDirectoryStorage for dev with tmp-dir tests; S3-storage stub documented, not integration-tested in MVP), persists a document registry as a JSON index (id, filename, sha256, size, uploaded_at, duplicate flag) and GET /documents list returning metadata; duplicate uploads with the same sha256 return the existing document record with duplicate=true and do not create registry copies. Routes registered on the main FastAPI app in backend/app/main.py via include_router; multipart upload requires python-multipart pinned in backend/pyproject.toml. Local-first, tests offline with tmp dirs (no network).
acceptance_criteria: POST /documents accepts pdf/md/txt, rejects unsupported extensions (400) and over-cap size (413), returns document id and metadata
GET /documents lists registered documents with metadata including sha256 and duplicate flag; identical sha256 re-upload is deduplicated (no new registry entry, duplicate=true response)
StorageBackend abstraction interface with LocalDirectoryStorage implementation covered by tmp-dir tests (content stored and retrievable; registry JSON persisted)
S3 storage stub documented in README but not required to be integration-tested in MVP
Deterministic test suite passes offline via python -m unittest discover -s tests -v from backend/ (and pytest); java-free, network-free
python-multipart added as pinned dependency in backend/pyproject.toml and documented in backend/README Setup note

tasks.title: RAG answer flow with citations and abstention
tasks.description: backend/app/rag.py: given a question, retrieve relevant chunks (chosen backend contract from RAG-BACKEND-SPIKE decision; local lexical/embedding retrieval as the local/testing path), build grounded answer with section-level citations, and abstain with INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when retrieval confidence/verdict is below threshold. POST /answer endpoint with {question} returning {answer, citations[], abstained}. Guarded by evaluation suite.
acceptance_criteria: POST /answer returns answer plus non-empty citations (doc id, section) for a in-scope golden question from the local retrieval path (offline tests)
Abstention: when retrieval yields no confident evidence, returns abstained=true with INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE and no fabricated citations; unit tests cover the threshold
Citations carry document id/section and retrieval score; answers never cite absent documents
Local retrieval implementation and tests run offline; Bedrock KB integration path behind interface and covered by integration flag if enabled
Existing document ingest integrated: newly uploaded doc becomes retrievable in tests

tasks.title: Evaluation harness with golden Q&A cases and regression gate
tasks.description: backend/app/eval.py + cases: YAML/JSON golden cases (question, expected source section, expected answer keywords); runner scores retrieval hit-rate and answer fidelity against the local retrieval path; CLI producing a JSON report; CI-friendly exit code failing on retrieval hit-rate regression below threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Golden case format documented and >= 5 cases defined incl. an expected-abstain case
Runner outputs JSON report with per-case retrieval hit and coverage/abstention rates
Exit code 0/n% threshold configurable; regression gate documented for CI use
Runner runs offline (local retrieval only) and is deterministic given a fixed index

tasks.title: Minimal Next.js chat UI with sources panel and document list
tasks.description: frontend/: minimal hand-rolled Next.js (App Router) scaffold - no create-next-app, no injection of unrelated template files: frontend/package.json (pinned deps react/next), frontend/app/layout.tsx (root layout), frontend/app/page.tsx (chat: question input POSTs to backend /answer, renders answer + citations panel with document/section locator + duplicate notice when abstained=true with INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE), frontend/app/documents/page.tsx (upload form POSTs multipart to backend /documents + lists metadata incl. sha256/duplicate), frontend/tests/test_smoke.py (scaffold-contract smoke test), frontend/README.md (run instructions, NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL env default http://localhost:8000, install/dev commands, known backend endpoints). Minimal inline styling; this unit ships no sign-in screen (user-identity screens are Month-2 scope); no CI. Node/npm availability at implementation time is recorded as evidence; if npm install cannot run offline the implementer records the exact failure and the UI is still delivered code-complete with build verification marked as residual/INSUFFICIENT honestly. The smoke test gives the frontend its OWN fast project test suite: the check-runner derives project root from task files, and a frontend/tests/ placement keeps the deterministic gate inside the frontend project (~0.1s) instead of resolving to the repository root whose full harness suite (~9-10 min measured) hangs under the runner's subprocess stdin model when run detached/captured (documented harness defect, backlog).
acceptance_criteria: Chat page sends question to backend /answer and renders answer plus citations list (doc/locator/score) when abstained=false; renders abstention notice when abstained=true
Documents page uploads a file (multipart) and lists metadata returned by backend (id, filename, sha256, size, duplicate)

Minimal manual Next.js scaffold: package.json parses as valid JSON with pinned react/next versions; app/ directory structure is a valid App Router layout (layout.tsx + pages compile under Next's expected tree)

frontend/tests/test_smoke.py validates the scaffold contract offline (no Node/network needed): package.json parses as JSON; layout.tsx/page.tsx contain the required markers (title, /answer call, abstained handling, citations render); documents page contains /documents call + FormData upload + metadata render; passes under python -m unittest discover -s tests -v and pytest from frontend/

Each page renders without runtime exceptions in a local build/dev attempt IF node is available; the implementer records the exact npm/node outcome (success or blocked) as durable evidence and documents residual if blocked - chromium/binary network fetches only due to npm install, never from page logic
README documents install, dev server run, backend base URL env (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL default http://localhost:8000) and known backend endpoints

proposed_sprint.goal: Weeks 1-2: healthy backend + LLM wrapper + document ingest (fast, low-risk, unblocks everything else).

recorded_decisions: roadmap requested explicitly by owner with 90-day plan and prioritization rule (small reliable product first)
Month-1 sprint materialized now; Month-2 and Month-3 epics stay as future work items with their own sprint planning
open questions explicitly non-blocking (region/cost ceiling, ticket vendor, domain - all needed only at later milestones)
